list.item: Term intrauterine pregnancy at 39 weeks 6 days.
Spontaneous rupture of membranes with early labor.
History of prior cesarean delivery followed by successful VBAC; desired repeat trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC).

text.paragraph: Mimi Shell was admitted on 10/14/2026 at 3:28 AM at 39w6d following spontaneous rupture of membranes at approximately 2:10 AM. She had one prior cesarean delivery followed by one successful VBAC and desired repeat TOLAC. Maternal and fetal status remained reassuring.

Care was initially provided by Rachel Morgan, MD and transferred to Emily Carter, MD in the morning. Labor progressed appropriately. Epidural analgesia was placed at approximately 12:30 PM. Mimi became complete at approximately 5:05 PM and delivered Lilly Anne Curic by spontaneous vaginal delivery at 5:45 PM, a successful repeat VBAC. Placenta delivered spontaneously and intact at approximately 5:53 PM. A small first-degree perineal laceration was repaired. No episiotomy was performed. Estimated blood loss was approximately 300 mL.

Postpartum recovery was uncomplicated. Mimi remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable with appropriate lochia and normal uterine involution. Pain was controlled with routine oral therapy and comfort measures. She ambulated, voided, tolerated diet, and independently participated in self-care and newborn care. Breastfeeding was established with routine lactation support available. She and Lilly Anne were discharged home together on 10/16/2026 at 11:18 AM.

list.item: Spontaneous vaginal delivery / successful repeat VBAC, 10/14/2026 5:45 PM.
Spontaneous intact placental delivery, approximately 5:53 PM.

text.paragraph: Admission evaluation included CBC and type-and-screen. No postpartum study requiring additional inpatient intervention is established in the synthetic scenario. Maternal clinical status remained reassuring through discharge.

Admission results on October 14, 2026: WBC 10.8 x10^3/uL; hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL; hematocrit 36.4%; platelets 218 x10^3/uL. Blood group O positive; antibody screen negative. No new postpartum thyroid result is asserted; thyroid reassessment is planned at approximately six weeks postpartum.

list.item: Status post spontaneous vaginal delivery / successful repeat VBAC at 39w6d.

text.paragraph: No known drug allergies are documented in the current synthetic scenario.

tr.td: Continue postpartum at pre-pregnancy dose. Thyroid function reassessment planned at approximately six weeks postpartum.

text.paragraph: Levothyroxine was reduced from the pregnancy dose of 125 mcg daily to the pre-pregnancy dose of 100 mcg daily beginning the morning of October 15. Mimi received 100 mcg on the mornings of October 15 and October 16. Continue 100 mcg daily after discharge.

At discharge Mimi is afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Lochia is appropriate and uterine involution is normal. Pain related to the repaired first-degree laceration is controlled with oral therapy and comfort measures. She is ambulating independently, voiding, tolerating diet, breastfeeding, and clinically appropriate for discharge home.

list.item: Continue routine postpartum recovery and breastfeeding/lactation support.
Continue levothyroxine 100 mcg PO daily; reassess thyroid function at approximately six weeks postpartum.
Follow up with Simone Heps at Health Services of North Texas on 10/30/2026 at 9:00 AM for the 2-week postpartum visit.
Return on 11/27/2026 at 9:00 AM for the 6-week comprehensive postpartum visit and thyroid reassessment.
Continue postpartum contraception and reproductive-life planning discussions during follow-up.
Ongoing maternal care transitions back to Simone Heps and Health Services of North Texas.

text.paragraph: Continue routine postpartum recovery, perineal care, breastfeeding support, hydration, nutrition, and gradual activity progression as instructed. Seek urgent evaluation for heavy bleeding, fever, severe or worsening headache, visual changes, chest pain, shortness of breath, severe abdominal pain, seizure, unilateral leg swelling or pain, or significant emotional or behavioral concerns.
